text:
Morgan: quick idea: introduce a 'soft SLA token bucket' for dedicated GPU pools. tenants declare soft targets (rps / p95) and we bank/ debit tokens instead of immediate hard eviction. aiming for graceful degradation instead of binary preempt
Arjun: sounds promising. how is this different from our current burst credits?
Morgan: burst credits = short-lived capacity tokens. soft SLA tokens = behavioral budget with a decay curve + admission probability impact. if you overshoot, we lower your future admission probability and slowly replenish, rather than evicting instantly
Kai: can you sketch the operator API for admission checks?
Morgan: operator would call control-plane: GetSlaBalance(tenant) -> {balance, last_updated, estimated_replenish_rate}. admission decision uses balance and pool headroom to compute admission_probability
Rebecca: who owns bookkeeping? operator or control-plane?
Morgan: control-plane owns accurate accounting and emits metrics. operator keeps a short-lived cache to avoid hot-path RPCs (TTL ~1s), and applies admission logic locally
Tess: what about spikes where a tenant legitimately needs burst capacity? we don't want them throttled for hours
Arjun: make it configurable: emergency_burst_ratio and grace_period. soft means probabilistic admission, not absolute block. e.g., emergency_burst_ratio=1.5 allows temporary overshoot but increases deficit
Kai: eviction policy? if pool under pressure we'd still need preemption for some jobs
Morgan: eviction scoring = sla_deficit * (1 + cost_factor) + recency_penalty. only evict preemptible / best-effort tasks. pinned/hard-sla jobs are immune
Rebecca: billing implications? do we bill for token burns or just report?
Morgan: initial plan: emit sla_tokens_burned{tenant,pool} as informational. billing/chargeback is optional follow-up; default is telemetry + quota gating
Tess: we should run a simulator to validate fairness across noisy tenants before rollout
Arjun: agreed. also feature-flag per-pool and staged rollout
Morgan: proposed rollout:
1) emit read-only metrics for 2 weeks
2) admission_probability mode (no evictions)
3) opt-in pools for live trials
4) enable enforcement + eviction heuristics
Kai: telemetry list suggestion: sla_tokens_balance (gauge), sla_tokens_burn_rate (counter), admission_probability (gauge), preempt_eviction_score (histogram), tenant_quality_regressions (counter)
ops-bot: checklist created: https://rwd/internal/ops/soft-sla-token-bucket/checklist
Rebecca: multi-tenant models: how do we attribute burn when a job serves multiple tenants?
Morgan: annotate incoming requests with tenant weight vector. attribute burn in proportion. anonymous traffic attributed to pool buffer; admins can set fallback policy
Tess: test plan: 20 tenants, 2 pools, synthetic ramps + spikes, validate that no tenant is starved and adopters keep p95 within soft bounds
Arjun: one concern: extra RPCs from operator to control-plane on hot path. can we cache aggressively?
Morgan: yes, cache 1s, adaptive backoff, and allow slightly stale balances for probabilistic admission. operator should fail-open to avoid blocking requests if control-plane unreachable (with admin override)
Kai: config example for pool YAML:
pool.soft_sla_enabled: true
pool.default_decay_half_life_hours: 6
pool.emergency_burst_ratio: 1.5
pool.admission_cache_ttl_seconds: 1
Rebecca: docs + SDK change: add client SDK helper to expose current admission_probability so infra teams can show graceful backpressure to app teams
Tess: add regression tests to RFC checklist; include small prompt sets that reproduce flaky p95s
Morgan: I'll draft RFC with simulator details, telemetry dashboard mocks, and phased rollout. ping if you want to co-author :thumbsup:
Arjun: follow-up sync next Wed 11am PT. tagging relevant folks for simulation pairing
